Prerequisites: 03 · Triangles, area and surface normals

Shape is not connectivity

Geometry tells us where vertices are; topology tells us how faces connect. Two vertices at the same position remain different vertices unless the index structure joins them. A visually closed surface can therefore contain disconnected seams. Conversely, moving vertices can badly deform a mesh while leaving every index and adjacency relation unchanged.

Each oriented triangle contributes three directed edges. Grouping their unordered endpoint pairs reveals shared edges. One incident face usually indicates a boundary. Two incident faces are the ordinary interior case for a manifold surface; consistent orientation traverses their common edge in opposite directions. More than two incident faces is an edge-level nonmanifold condition. Edge checks alone do not prove a surface manifold at every vertex: a pinched vertex can join disconnected surface fans.

Worked example

A square split along one diagonal has four vertices, five distinct edges and two faces, giving characteristic one. Its four outer edges have one incident face; its diagonal has two. A tetrahedron's surface has four vertices, six edges and four faces, giving characteristic two. The difference does not mean the square is broken: it is a surface with a boundary rather than a closed sphere-like surface.

Duplicate faces, repeated corner indices, out-of-range indices, nonfinite positions and inconsistent winding are different defects. A validator should name what it checked. “No errors found” is misleading if a costly geometric survey was disabled. An index may be in the global vertex array yet belong to the wrong mesh in a packed batch; offsets therefore carry semantic ownership, not just convenient slicing.

Try it yourself

If every vertex position in the square is moved randomly, must its Euler characteristic change?

Answer

No, provided the same vertices, edges and faces remain. The resulting shape may self-intersect or collapse, but combinatorial counts have not changed.

gffx boundary

build_edge_topology and validate expose existing structural tools. The validation report is a survey, not permission for later kernels to skip safety checks. Optional geometry checks must not be reported as measured when they were not requested. Topology and index selection are discrete; gradients through moving vertices do not amount to gradients through creating or deleting faces. Automatic remeshing, general mesh repair and complete self-intersection diagnosis are not implied by these baseline operations.
